scope: Owner-facing application creation, credential revocation and irreversible retirement API/UI, plus bot gateway revocation race closure.
implemented: Bot WebSocket admission now waits until the Hub has indexed the connection and then revalidates the exact credential. A retirement/revocation committed during admission closes the socket with code 4001 before pumps begin.

Active bot sockets revalidate the credential on keepalive. Same-process credential revocation disconnects the owned bot immediately after the durable transaction; other processes fail closed at periodic revalidation.

The production repository and authentication service now include application removal. POST /api/bots/{botID}/remove binds the active human account, session and path identity; uses a bounded strict JSON body; requires password, current MFA when enabled, a separate checkbox and exact REMOVE text; and never mutates login cookies.

Bot identity plus initial token hash are created in one transaction. Token persistence failure rolls back the identity, while the plaintext credential is returned only after commit and shown only in transient UI state.

Token revocation proves current ownership and updates token tombstones in one transaction. Foreign/missing targets return not found and are never disconnected; repeated revocation of an owned bot stays idempotent.

Account settings now have a Turkish/English Applications and bots panel with real list/create, one-time token handling, explicit revoke, and irreversible retirement. It guards late responses by account generation and preserves uncertain-state warnings instead of reporting success.

Account deletion resource cards route owned applications to the real management panel. Shared history retention and queued personal-asset cleanup are checked in both the API acknowledgement and the UI before reporting removal success.
The OpenAPI contract and route golden include the human-only removal operation and its explicit consent/error behavior.
